27 Sound waves of wavelength λ are emitted by a loudspeaker and pass through two slits P and Q.
Two sound waves from the slits meet at R.
R
microphone
P
Q
loudspeaker
sound barrier
with two slits
What is the condition for an intensity maximum (loud sound) to be detected by a microphone
at R?
A
The amplitudes of the two waves at R must be the same.
B
The distance PQ must be smaller than the wavelength λ.
C
The two waves from the slits must have travelled the same distance to R.
D
The two waves must be in phase at R.

hints: Notice the microphone at R receives one wave diffracted from P and one wave diffracted from Q, so the loudness depends on their superposition at R.
Recall that constructive superposition for two coherent sound waves needs crest to add to crest and compression to add to compression at R.
Check whether equal path lengths PR and QR is the only way to get that addition, or whether a path difference of $\lambda$, $2\lambda$ and so on can do it too.
walkthrough: Identify the set-up: the single loudspeaker illuminates slits P and Q, so P and Q act as two coherent sources of wavelength $\lambda$ whose waves overlap at R.
State the superposition rule: the resultant displacement at R is the vector sum of the two wave displacements, and intensity is maximum when this sum has largest magnitude.
Maximum resultant occurs with constructive interference, when the two displacements always point in the same direction at R.
That same-direction condition is that the phase difference at R is $0$ or a whole number of cycles, meaning the waves are in phase at R.
Equal distances would give zero path difference, which is only one example; a path difference of $n\lambda$ also gives in-phase arrival away from the centre. This is option D.

A.explanation: Equal amplitudes at R improve contrast between loud and quiet positions but are not required for a maximum to occur.

B.explanation: Slit separation PQ affects spreading and fringe spacing, but the condition for loud sound at R depends on the waves arriving at R, not on PQ being less than $\lambda$.

C.explanation: Equal distances PR and QR give zero path difference and one maximum, but maxima also occur where the path difference is $n\lambda$.

D.explanation: In-phase arrival means compressions meet compressions so displacements add constructively to give maximum intensity.
